title: Seasons in the County
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 4 Social Studies; not yet checked by a CBC Social Studies teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Keep a class weather chart for two weeks before this sub-strand and use it. The seasons are named as the county knows them; long and short rains differ across Kenya, so the teacher confirms the months for the school's county.

skills.key_step: The child names the four local seasons (hot, cold, dry, rainy) from their weather and knows a season lasts many weeks.

floor.question: What is the weather like now?
floor.answer: any of: sunny, rainy, cloudy, windy, cold

representations: the class weather chart for two weeks
a circle calendar with the months
pictures of each season in the county
steps: Read the weather of many days on the chart.
Group days of the same weather into weeks.
Name the season the weeks make.
contexts: the long rains around March to May
a cold July morning in the highlands
dust and heat before the rains in the lowlands

board.do: Draw a circle split into twelve months.

board.say: What weather do many counties get in these months?

board.do: Ask which months come before: wet or dry?

misconceptions.ask: Which of these is a season in our county?
misconceptions.repair: Ask the child to name the weather of each month of the school year, then give each stretch its own name.

misconceptions.ask: When there is little rain and no clouds for many days, which season is it?
misconceptions.repair: Make a weather chart over a week and name the season from what it shows.

listen_for: It is now the rainy season
misconceptions.ask: It rained on Tuesday. What can we say?
misconceptions.repair: Ask what the weather was every day of one month, then name the season.

listen_for: Yes, it rains at the same time everywhere
misconceptions.ask: Is the rainy season in the same months in every part of Kenya?
misconceptions.repair: Compare the class chart with a chart from another region read out by the teacher.

checks.question: Name the four seasons in the county.
It rained heavily on one day in January. Is January the rainy season?
checks.answer: No: one rainy day is weather, a season lasts many weeks

skills.key_step: The child links each season to what people do: plant at the start of the rains, harvest and dry in the dry season, wear warm clothes in the cold.

floor.prerequisite: Names the four seasons and their weather.
floor.question: Which season has the most rain?

representations: a season wheel with activities drawn on it
a sort: activity cards into season boxes
steps: Say what people need or can do in that weather.
Check the activity fits the weather.
contexts: planting maize when the long rains begin
selling cold drinks at a hot bus stage
wearing sweaters in the cold season in Nyandarua

board.do: Draw a farmer with a jembe and clouds above.

board.say: Is this a good time to plant? Why?

board.do: Wait for the child to say the rain wets the soil.
Draw maize drying on a mat in the sun.
Write "dry season: dry and store the harvest".

misconceptions.repair: Plant two cups of beans, water one, and compare after a week.

misconceptions.ask: What do people wear in the cold season?
misconceptions.repair: Ask what the child wears on a cold morning and what on a hot afternoon.

listen_for: No, people do the same all year
misconceptions.ask: Do seasons change what people do?
misconceptions.repair: Ask what changes at home when the rains start: crops, roads, clothes, school trips.

misconceptions.ask: When do farmers dry and store their maize?
misconceptions.repair: Ask what happens to maize left out to dry in the rain: it rots.

checks.question: Why do farmers plant at the start of the rainy season?
checks.answer: The rain wets the soil so seeds can grow

checks.question: Which activity fits the cold season: drying maize, wearing warm clothes, swimming?

skills.key_step: The child says how rain makes roads dangerous and picks the safe action: wait, never cross flood water, never run, be seen.

floor.prerequisite: Knows basic road signs and safety on the road.
floor.question: Where should you cross a road?
floor.answer: at a zebra crossing or where you can see both ways, after looking right, left and right again

representations: a picture of a wet road with a puddle and a matatu
a role play of crossing in the rain
steps: Say what the rain does to the road: slippery, muddy, flooded.
Say what it does to seeing: hard for drivers and walkers.
Say why the unsafe one is dangerous.
contexts: a flooded drift on the way home
a busy road in an evening storm

board.do: Draw a road with water running across it and a child at the edge.

board.say: Should the child walk through it?

board.do: Wait for the child to answer and give a reason.
Show that moving water can be deeper and stronger than it looks.

listen_for: Run across fast to get out of the rain
misconceptions.ask: It is raining. What should Njeri do at the road?
misconceptions.repair: Role play crossing in the rain: slow, look both ways, hold a friend's hand.

listen_for: Cross if the water looks shallow
misconceptions.ask: A road has water flowing across it after heavy rain. What should you do?
misconceptions.repair: Show a picture of a drift in flood; ask what is hidden under the water.

listen_for: Faster, to get out of the rain
misconceptions.ask: How should a driver drive in heavy rain?
misconceptions.repair: Ask how long it takes to stop on a slippery floor when you run.

listen_for: Dark clothes and an umbrella over the face
misconceptions.ask: It is raining heavily in the evening. What helps drivers see a walker?
misconceptions.repair: In a dim room, hold up a dark cloth and a bright one: which do you see first?

checks.question: Flood water covers the road home. It looks shallow. What should you do?
checks.answer: Wait in a safe place or find an adult; never cross

checks.question: Why must drivers slow down in the rain?
checks.answer: The road is slippery and it is hard to see
